diagnosis_contract.confirmed: R130's mass-metric tangent projection is numerically valid but its resulting fixed-PD input schedule violates the frozen right-ankle-roll actuator limits before inverse dynamics
diagnosis_contract.supported_hotspot: the four largest R130 corrections occupy substeps 2/3 of exit intervals 76 and 744, both right forefoot to flight
diagnosis_contract.not_claimed: R130 emitted no projected vectors or controller-event row indices, so exact row-to-violation identity and inverse-dynamics feasibility remain unknown
diagnosis_contract.smallest_question: does importing the next flight knot velocity into a still-active exit interval cause the actuator-invalid late correction?

current_cross_mode_lift_contract.configuration: q(i,u) is independently interpolated from exact knots q_i and q_(i+1)
current_cross_mode_lift_contract.contact_mode: the left interval mode A_i owns all four collocations
current_cross_mode_lift_contract.motor_boundary_reanchor: interval i+1 starts from exact knot v_(i+1)
current_cross_mode_lift_contract.problem_at_exit: for A_i active and A_(i+1) flight, u>0 mixes flight-side v_(i+1) into rows still constrained by A_i

alternative_decisions.reason: R130 falsifies actuator-schedule preservation and its largest corrections cluster where the right endpoint belongs to flight
it removes only future flight-velocity contamination from nine contact-exit intervals and yields a 36-row falsifiable anchor set
a pointwise velocity box does not by itself close qdot identity or sequential effort-rate, power and work state
joint q, v, a, effort and contact-force variables address integration and actuator feasibility but materially widen the intervention
it changes current rigid mode ownership and requires an explicit backend correspondence contract

selected_edge_lift_contract.name: exit_mode_owned_left_velocity_trace_hold
selected_edge_lift_contract.selection_predicate: an interval i is selected iff any foot mode is nonzero in A_i and zero in A_(i+1)
selected_edge_lift_contract.ordinary_interval_velocity_weights: at substep s use endpoint numerators [4-s,s] over denominator 4
selected_edge_lift_contract.selected_exit_interval_velocity_weights: at every substep s use endpoint numerators [4,0] over denominator 4
selected_edge_lift_contract.substep_zero_identity: selected and current lifts are byte-identical at u=0
selected_edge_lift_contract.changed_rows: only substeps 1/2/3 of the nine selected exit intervals may change before projection
selected_edge_lift_contract.right_boundary_reanchor: the next interval starts from exact v_(i+1); the diagnostic permits an explicit mode-boundary velocity trace discontinuity
selected_edge_lift_contract.configuration: retain R121 affine translation/joint configuration and SO(3) root interpolation byte-for-byte
selected_edge_lift_contract.contact_schedule: retain every R121/R130 mode and active point byte-for-byte
selected_edge_lift_contract.target_schedule: retain every R121/R130 fixed-PD target, gain and descriptor safety limit byte-for-byte
selected_edge_lift_contract.projection: apply the already-conformed R129 mass-metric tangent projection against A_i after selecting the base velocity
selected_edge_lift_contract.controller_observation: use the same ties-to-even joint position/velocity quantization and fixed-PD schedule rules as R130
selected_edge_lift_contract.promotion_ceiling: a later schedule PASS would isolate the edge-lift cause but would not establish integration, impact, inverse-dynamics, PhysX or corpus feasibility

R129 rank, KKT, tangent, idempotence, energy and gauge bounds on every selected row
row-addressed pre/post projection joint velocity and correction evidence
synthetic ordinary, entry, active-mode-change, exit and malformed-edge cases
